text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.07% today and has climbed 20.7% over the past two weeks, driven primarily by a sharp spike in oil and diesel prices amid escalating Middle East tensions. Reports of attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and Iran's threats against U.S. assets have pushed global crude to $125.44 per barrel (compared to U.S. domestic oil at $96.24), and forecasts of tight diesel supplies into 2027 directly benefit refiners—who profit from the spread between crude input costs and refined product output. With U.S. refineries running at 92.7% capacity and diesel inventories lean at 105.1 million barrels, the company is well-positioned to capture margin gains in a supply-constrained environment.

The stock's two-week gain reflects the cumulative effect of geopolitical risk premiums layered onto existing supply tightness. Ukraine and Iran conflicts are creating persistent disruptions to global energy flows, and with the IEA warning of structural constraints, refiners' ability to convert crude into high-demand diesel at favorable margins remains a key tailwind for profitability.
